sentences.text: The genus Dasosaurus includes a single species, Dasosaurus tocantinensis.
The holotype — the specimen on which the species is based — indicates a medium-to-large sauropod about 20 meters in length.
Archaeologist Daniel Ribeiro da Silva uncovered the fossils in Davinópolis, Maranhão, Brazil.
The find was announced in 2021 as representing a new titanosaur taxon.
The generic name combines Greek terms for “forest” and “lizard,” alluding to the Amazon rainforest setting.
The specific epithet tocantinensis honors the nearby state of Tocantins.
The holotype material comprises limb bones, ribs, and at least ten disarticulated tail vertebrae.
Its overall shape resembles that of the European titanosauriform Garumbatitan.
It is placed within the sauropod clade Somphospondyli, a subgroup of the larger Saurischia class.
Dasosaurus lived in the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
Some researchers argue that the European affinities of Dasosaurus suggest biogeographic links between Brazil and Europe during the Early Cretaceous.
